gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the Algorithm 2 comparison as incorrectly comparing the angular distance d with the cosine value 1/sqrt(n) instead of the conjectured angle arccos(1/sqrt(n)). They also identify the resulting misclassification of extremal inputs and prescribe replacing the scale in both tests.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Algorithm 2 uses the wrong numerical scale in its extremality predicates: an angular quantity is compared against 1/sqrt(n), rather than against theta_n = arccos(1/sqrt(n)). This causes exact extremal subspaces to be rejected and can misclassify other values.

component_coverage.gold_component: Algorithm 2 centers both upper and lower extremality tests at the wrong scale, comparing the angular distance d with 1/sqrt(n) rather than theta_n = arccos(1/sqrt(n)), causing incorrect classification of extremal and nonextremal candidates.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that d is an angle, that the algorithm compares it with the cosine 1/sqrt(n), gives the inequality showing extremal subspaces are wrongly rejected, and supplies the specific correction arccos(1/sqrt(n)) in both conditions.
